title: Investment in the Contract on Income Annuities Arrears Installments: Annuitized and IRA Contracts
content:
The tax-free part of an arrears installment paid to the beneficiary on an Ashgrove Income Annuities period-certain contract is never more than the investment in the contract less the tax-free amount already recovered on the contract, and never less than zero. For two kinds of contract, the investment in the contract is fixed as follows.

| Contract, as its income annuity record shows it | Investment in the contract |
|---|---|
| Bought by annuitizing an Ashgrove fixed indexed annuity (a Fixed Indexed Annuities contract) or an Ashgrove deferred fixed annuity (a Deferred Fixed Annuities contract) | The cost basis of the annuity annuitized |
| A traditional IRA or SEP IRA not bought by annuitizing an Ashgrove deferred annuity | Zero |

For an Income Annuities contract in neither situation, this table does not apply.

**Where the figures are found.** The income annuity contract record shows the purchase source (annuitization of an Ashgrove fixed indexed annuity, annuitization of an Ashgrove deferred fixed annuity, new money, exchange, transfer or rollover), the reference of the annuitized contract and the tax qualification. The cost basis is read from the record of the annuitized Fixed Indexed Annuities or Deferred Fixed Annuities contract itself.

**Illustrations (hypothetical).**

- *Annuitized deferred fixed annuity.* Cost basis on the Deferred Fixed Annuities contract $120,000.00; tax-free amount already recovered on the income contract $119,700.00; installment $1,000.00 with an exclusion ratio of 64.86%. The installment multiplied by the ratio is $648.60, but only $300.00 of the investment remains unrecovered, so the tax-free part is $300.00 and the taxable part $700.00.
- *Annuitized fixed indexed annuity, investment fully recovered.* Cost basis $90,000.00, already recovered $90,000.00: nothing remains, so the tax-free part is zero and the whole installment is taxable.
- *Traditional IRA funded with new money.* Investment zero: the tax-free part can never be more than zero, so the whole arrears installment is taxable.
